body:
I'll start by reading the shared contract and manifests, then verify source lines before writing.

Now let me verify source lines for chapter 06 (typing core). I'll batch searches.

I have the core lines. Let me verify a few uncertain line numbers before writing.

Now I'll write all four chapters with verified citations.

Chapter 07 is under the byte minimum; I'll expand it with verified content.

Now let me verify all four files against the contract with a local checker.

All four chapters are written and pass the shared contract checks locally.

| File | Bytes | Citations | Tables | URLs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `06-static-typing-core.md` | 7,049 | 45 | 3 | 7 |
| `07-static-typing-workflow.md` | 6,019 | 28 | 4 | 7 |
| `08-data-modeling.md` | 6,350 | 41 | 3 | 6 |
| `09-errors-and-exception-groups.md` | 5,841 | 30 | 2 | 6 |

Total: 144 line-cited `samples/<file>:LINE` tokens, all pointing to existing files with in-range lines. Each file has the exact `# NN - Title` first line, a final `## Sources` section with ≥5 official URLs, balanced language-tagged fences under 25 lines, no Portuguese leakage, and no placeholder markers.

Facts deliberately left `not verified`:
- `Unknown` type semantics (ch. 06) — no captured line defines it.
- `ty` from Astral (ch. 07) — no captured line mentions it; no config shown.
- Whether any specific installed dependency ships a `py.typed` marker (ch. 07) — environment-specific.
- `Result`-style return type (ch. 09) — no captured source defines one.

Checker config flags (mypy/pyright/basedpyright) and rollout/CI rules are explicitly labelled `derived`; the wiki exception-handling fact is labelled `wiki, lower authority`.
